builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Instrumental Variables in Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
summary: The method replaces maximum-likelihood estimation and discrete-time IV approaches for identifying causal effects in continuous-time systems with unobserved confounding, using path-valued instruments and moment restrictions on SDE drift structure. Cost is moderate statistical and implementation complexity, including signature-kernel computation for nonlinear effects, but it runs on ordinary hardware. It can fail if the identification condition is unmet, if a valid instrumental process is unavailable, or if the stationarity and structural sparsity assumptions do not hold.
rationale: This is a causal-inference method for stochastic differential equations, not an LLM efficiency or agent technique, and it is only relevant if the reader works on causal estimation in continuous-time dynamical systems.
technique: Instrumental variables for continuous-time SDE causal inference

claims.statement: The method replaces maximum-likelihood estimation and discrete-time IV approaches for identifying causal effects in continuous-time systems with unobserved confounding, using path-valued instruments and moment restrictions on SDE drift structure. Cost is moderate statistical and implementation complexity, including signature-kernel computation for nonlinear effects, but it runs on ordinary hardware. It can fail if the identification condition is unmet, if a valid instrumental process is unavailable, or if the stationarity and structural sparsity assumptions do not hold.
Empirically recovers causal effects in confounded continuous-time systems where maximum-likelihood estimation and discrete-time IV methods are systematically biased; no quantitative factor reported.
